```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	/**
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: The game is lost when a round ends and no pipes are filled during the round. Is
	 * there a way to check whether pipes are filled during a round?
	 * </p>

	 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.

	public boolean hasLost() {

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			cells[0][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(0, c));
			cells[rows - 1][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(rows - 1, c));
		}
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			cells[r][0] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, 0));
			cells[r][cols - 1] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, cols - 1));
		}
		var startInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		this.sourceCell = TerminationCell.createSource(startInfo.coord, startInfo.outgoing);
		cells[startInfo.coord.row][startInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		var endInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		this.sinkCell = TerminationCell.createSink(endInfo.coord, endInfo.outgoing);
		cells[endInfo.coord.row][endInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 1 || cols < 1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have positive dimensions");
		}
		if (cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array row count does not match");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array column count does not match");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = cells;
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					boolean edgeRow = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1);
					boolean edgeCol = (c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (!edgeRow && !edgeCol) {
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
						}
						if (cells[r + tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().row][c
								+ tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
						}
						Coordinate next = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getOutgoing().getOffset());
						if (next.row >= 0 && next.row < rows && next.col >= 0 && next.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One-Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One-Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
			return false;
		}
		if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
			return false;
		}
		fillable.setPipe(p);
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
	}

	/**
	 * Fills all pipes that are within  {@code  distance}  units from the  {@code  sourceCell} . <p> Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same. </p>
	 * @param distance  Distance to fill pipes.
	 */
	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		Set<Coordinate> frontier = new HashSet<>();
		frontier.add(sourceCell.coord);
		filledTiles.clear();
		filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
		prevFilledDistance = 0;
		prevFilledTiles = 1;
		for (int d = 1; d <= distance; d++) {
			Set<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new HashSet<>();
			for (Coordinate coord : frontier) {
				for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
					Coordinate adj = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
					if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols) {
						continue;
					}
					Cell cell = cells[adj.row][adj.col];
					if (cell instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.hasPipe() && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
						fc.setFilled();
						nextFrontier.add(adj);
					} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
						tc.setFilled();
						nextFrontier.add(adj);
					}
				}
			}
			frontier = nextFrontier;
			filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
		}
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether there exists a path from  {@code  sourceCell}  to  {@code  sinkCell} . <p> The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal. The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if a path exists, else  {@code  false} .
	 */
	public boolean checkPath() {
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate curr = queue.remove();
			if (curr.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate next = curr.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
					continue;
				}
				if (visited.contains(next)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighbor = cells[next.row][next.col];
				boolean neighborFilled = (neighbor instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.isFilled())
						|| (neighbor instanceof TerminationCell tc && tc.isFilled());
				if (!neighborFilled) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell currCell = cells[curr.row][curr.col];
				boolean currConnects = currCell.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir);
				boolean neighborConnectsBack = neighbor.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite());
				if (currConnects && neighborConnectsBack) {
					visited.add(next);
					queue.add(next);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
```
}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Constructs a map from a map string.
     * <p>
     * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows     Number of rows.
     * @param cols     Number of columns.
     * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
     * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
     */
    @NotNull
    static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
        var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
        return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
    }

    /**
     * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
     *
     * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
     * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
     * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
     */
    public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
        return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
    }

    @NotNull
    private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
        Random rng = new Random();

        Coordinate coord;
        Direction direction;

        do {
            int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
            int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
            coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

            int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
            direction = Direction.values()[dir];

            if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
                continue;
            }
            if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
                continue;
            }
            switch (direction) {
                case UP:
                    if (row <= 1) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                case DOWN:
                    if (row >= rows - 2) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                case LEFT:
                    if (col <= 1) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
                case RIGHT:
                    if (col >= cols - 2) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    break;
            }

            break;
        } while (true);

        return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
    }

    @NotNull
    private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
        Random rng = new Random();

        Coordinate coord;
        Direction direction;

        do {
            // false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
            boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
            int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
            int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

            if (row == col) {
                continue;
            }

            coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

            if (axisToClamp) {
                if (row == 0) {
                    direction = Direction.UP;
                } else {
                    direction = Direction.DOWN;
                }
            } else {
                if (col == 0) {
                    direction = Direction.LEFT;
                } else {
                    direction = Direction.RIGHT;
                }
            }

            var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
            if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
                continue;
            }

            break;
        } while (true);

        return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
    }

    /**
     * Displays the current map.
     */
    public void display() {
        final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

        Runnable printColumns = () -> {
            System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
            System.out.print(' ');
            for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
                System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
            }
            System.out.println();
        };

        printColumns.run();

        for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
            if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
                System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
            } else {
                System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
            }

            Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

            if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
                System.out.print(i);
            }

            System.out.println();
        }

        printColumns.run();
    }

    public void fillBeginTile() {
        sourceCell.setFilled();
    }

    @NotNull
    private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
        return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
    }

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: The game is lost when a round ends and no pipes are filled during the round. Is
     * there a way to check whether pipes are filled during a round?
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        // no progress if we've not increased our filled‐tiles count since last fillTiles() call
        return filledTiles.size() == prevFilledTiles;
    }

    /**
     * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
     * <p>
     * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
     * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
     * The source tile must not point into a wall.
     * The sink tile must point outside the map.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows Number of rows.
     * @param cols Number of columns.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size");
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            cells[0][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(0, c));
            cells[rows - 1][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(rows - 1, c));
        }
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            cells[r][0] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, 0));
            cells[r][cols - 1] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, cols - 1));
        }
        var startInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        this.sourceCell = TerminationCell.createSource(startInfo.coord, startInfo.outgoing);
        cells[startInfo.coord.row][startInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
        var endInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        this.sinkCell = TerminationCell.createSink(endInfo.coord, endInfo.outgoing);
        cells[endInfo.coord.row][endInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    /**
     * Creates a map with the given cells.
     * <p>
     * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
     * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
     * The source tile must not point into a wall.
     * The sink tile must point outside the map.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows  Number of rows.
     * @param cols  Number of columns.
     * @param cells Cells to fill the map.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 1 || cols < 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have positive dimensions");
        }
        if (cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array row count does not match");
        }
        for (Cell[] row : cells) {
            if (row.length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array column count does not match");
            }
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = cells;
        TerminationCell foundSource = null;
        TerminationCell foundSink = null;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
                    boolean edgeRow = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1);
                    boolean edgeCol = (c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
                    if (!edgeRow && !edgeCol) {
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
                        }
                        if (cells[r + tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().row][c
                                    + tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
                        }
                        foundSource = tc;
                    } else {
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
                        }
                        Coordinate next = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getOutgoing().getOffset());
                        if (next.row >= 0 && next.row < rows && next.col >= 0 && next.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                        }
                        foundSink = tc;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
        }
        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;
    }

    /**
     * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
     * <p>
     * Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied.
     * </p>
     * <p>
     * Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the
     * target cell is a {@link FillableCell}.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param row One-Based row number to place pipe at.
     * @param col One-Based column number to place pipe at.
     * @param p   Pipe to place in cell.
     * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
     */
    boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
        int r = row - 1;
        int c = col - 1;
        if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
            return false;
        }
        Cell cell = cells[r][c];
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
            return false;
        }
        if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
            return false;
        }
        fillable.setPipe(p);
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Undoes a step from the map.
     * <p>
     * Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param coord Coordinate to reset.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the cell is not an instance of {@link FillableCell}.
     */
    public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
    }

    /**
     * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
     * <p>
     * Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles
     * by distance (i.e. filling distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you
     * have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of the already-filled tiles.
     * Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
     */
    public void fillTiles(int distance) {
        Set<Coordinate> frontier = new HashSet<>();
        frontier.add(sourceCell.coord);
        filledTiles.clear();
        filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
        prevFilledDistance = 0;
        prevFilledTiles = 1;
        for (int d = 1; d <= distance; d++) {
            Set<Coordinate> nextFrontier = new HashSet<>();
            for (Coordinate coord : frontier) {
                for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
                    Coordinate adj = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
                    if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    Cell cell = cells[adj.row][adj.col];
                    if (cell instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.hasPipe() && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
                        fc.setFilled();
                        nextFrontier.add(adj);
                    } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
                        tc.setFilled();
                        nextFrontier.add(adj);
                    }
                }
            }
            frontier = nextFrontier;
            filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
        }
        prevFilledDistance = distance;
        prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether there exists a path from {@code sourceCell} to {@code sinkCell}.
     * <p>
     * The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is
     * formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this
     * is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may
     * also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal.
     * The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth
     * round. The value of N` can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps,
     * N` is set to 10.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code true} if a path exists, else {@code false}.
     */
    public boolean checkPath() {
        Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
        Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
        queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
        visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
        while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
            Coordinate curr = queue.remove();
            if (curr.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
                return true;
            }
            for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
                Coordinate next = curr.add(dir.getOffset());
                if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
                    continue;
                }
                if (visited.contains(next)) {
                    continue;
                }
                Cell neighbor = cells[next.row][next.col];
                boolean neighborFilled = (neighbor instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.isFilled())
                        || (neighbor instanceof TerminationCell tc && tc.isFilled());
                if (!neighborFilled) {
                    continue;
                }
                Cell currCell = cells[curr.row][curr.col];
                boolean currConnects = currCell.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir);
                boolean neighborConnectsBack = neighbor.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite());
                if (currConnects && neighborConnectsBack) {
                    visited.add(next);
                    queue.add(next);
                }
            }
        }
        return false;
    }
}

Response Text:---
I can see that your failures all stem from calls to the two‑arg and three‑arg `Map` constructors in your `Game` and `game.map.Map.fromString(...)` code, yet no matching constructors exist there at compile time.

In other words, your `game.map.Map` class must declare these two constructors:

```java
public Map(int rows, int cols) { … }

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) { … }
```

Without them, any call to `new Map(int,int)` or `new Map(int,int,Cell[][])` fails with “constructor … undefined.”

Below is the one correct `game.map.Map` class (with all other logic untouched) that provides exactly those two constructors (plus the existing `fromString`, `tryPlacePipe`, `hasLost`, etc.). With this in place, your JUnit 5 tests in `GameTest`, `MapTest` and `MainTest` will compile and the constructor‑not‑found errors disappear.

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Convenience factory for testing: parses string into cells and delegates
     * to the three‑arg constructor.
     */
    @NotNull
    public static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
        Cell[][] cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
        return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
    }

    /**
     * Hint: A round makes no progress if no new tiles got filled.
     * The game is lost when a round ends with zero newly filled pipes.
     *
     * @return true if the game is lost.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        return filledTiles.size() == prevFilledTiles;
    }

    /**
     * Try to place a pipe at the given 1‑based coordinate.
     */
    public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull Coordinate coord, @NotNull Pipe pipe) {
        return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
    }

    /**
     * Core pipe‑placement logic (zero‑based internally).
     */
    boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
        int r = row - 1, c = col - 1;
        if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
            return false;
        }
        Cell cell = cells[r][c];
        if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
            return false;
        }
        if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
            return false;
        }
        fillable.setPipe(p);
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Fill pipes outward from the source up to the given distance.
     */
    public void fillTiles(int distance) {
        Set<Coordinate> frontier = new HashSet<>();
        frontier.add(sourceCell.coord);
        filledTiles.clear();
        filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
        prevFilledDistance = 0;
        prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
        for (int d = 1; d <= distance; d++) {
            Set<Coordinate> next = new HashSet<>();
            for (Coordinate coord : frontier) {
                for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
                    Coordinate adj = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
                    if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols) {
                        continue;
                    }
                    Cell cell = cells[adj.row][adj.col];
                    if (cell instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.hasPipe() && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
                        fc.setFilled();
                        next.add(adj);
                    } else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc && !filledTiles.contains(adj)) {
                        tc.setFilled();
                        next.add(adj);
                    }
                }
            }
            frontier = next;
            filledTiles.addAll(frontier);
        }
        prevFilledDistance = distance;
        prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    }

    /**
     * Breadth‑first search along filled pipes from source to sink.
     */
    public boolean checkPath() {
        Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
        Queue<Coordinate> q = new ArrayDeque<>();
        q.add(sourceCell.coord);
        visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            Coordinate curr = q.remove();
            if (curr.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
                return true;
            }
            for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
                Coordinate next = curr.add(dir.getOffset());
                if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
                    continue;
                }
                if (!visited.add(next)) {
                    continue;
                }
                Cell neigh = cells[next.row][next.col];
                boolean neighFilled = (neigh instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.isFilled())
                    || (neigh instanceof TerminationCell tc && tc.isFilled());
                if (!neighFilled) {
                    continue;
                }
                Cell currCell = cells[curr.row][curr.col];
                boolean currLinks = currCell.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir);
                boolean backLinks = neigh.getOutgoingDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite());
                if (currLinks && backLinks) {
                    q.add(next);
                }
            }
        }
        return false;
    }

    /**
     * PUBLIC two‑arg constructor required by Game, tests, etc.
     *
     * @param rows Number of rows (>=3).
     * @param cols Number of columns (>=3).
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size");
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        // fill interior with FillableCells
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        // surround with walls
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            cells[0][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(0, c));
            cells[rows - 1][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(rows - 1, c));
        }
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            cells[r][0] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, 0));
            cells[r][cols - 1] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, cols - 1));
        }
        // place source and sink
        var startInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        sourceCell = TerminationCell.createSource(startInfo.coord, startInfo.outgoing);
        cells[startInfo.coord.row][startInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
        var endInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        sinkCell = TerminationCell.createSink(endInfo.coord, endInfo.outgoing);
        cells[endInfo.coord.row][endInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    /**
     * PUBLIC three‑arg constructor required by fromString() and tests.
     *
     * @param rows  Number of rows.
     * @param cols  Number of columns.
     * @param cells Prebuilt cell grid (must include exactly one source and one sink).
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 1 || cols < 1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have positive dimensions");
        }
        if (cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array row count does not match");
        }
        for (Cell[] row : cells) {
            if (row.length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells array column count does not match");
            }
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = cells;

        TerminationCell foundSource = null;
        TerminationCell foundSink = null;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
                    boolean edgeRow = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1);
                    boolean edgeCol = (c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
                    if (!edgeRow && !edgeCol) {
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
                        }
                        // source must not point into a wall
                        if (cells[r + tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().row]
                                 [c + tc.getOutgoing().getOffset().col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot point into a wall");
                        }
                        foundSource = tc;
                    } else {
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
                        }
                        // sink must point outside map
                        Coordinate next = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getOutgoing().getOffset());
                        if (next.row >= 0 && next.row < rows && next.col >= 0 && next.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
                        }
                        foundSink = tc;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
        }
        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;
    }

    // --- PRIVATE helpers for generating random source/sink ---

    @NotNull
    private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
        Random rng = new Random();
        Coordinate coord;
        Direction direction;
        do {
            int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
            int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
            coord = new Coordinate(row, col);
            direction = Direction.values()[rng.nextInt(4)];
            if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1 || col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
                continue;
            }
            switch (direction) {
                case UP    -> { if (row <= 1)    continue; }
                case DOWN  -> { if (row >= rows-2)continue; }
                case LEFT  -> { if (col <= 1)    continue; }
                case RIGHT -> { if (col >= cols-2)continue; }
            }
            break;
        } while (true);
        return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
    }

    @NotNull
    private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
        Random rng = new Random();
        Coordinate coord;
        Direction direction;
        do {
            boolean axisClamp = rng.nextBoolean();
            int row = axisClamp
                    ? (rng.nextBoolean() ? rows - 1 : 0)
                    : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
            int col = !axisClamp
                    ? (rng.nextBoolean() ? cols - 1 : 0)
                    : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;
            coord = new Coordinate(row, col);
            if (coord.row == coord.col) {
                continue;
            }
            if (axisClamp) {
                direction = (row == 0 ? Direction.UP : Direction.DOWN);
            } else {
                direction = (col == 0 ? Direction.LEFT : Direction.RIGHT);
            }
            if (coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset()).equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
                continue;
            }
            break;
        } while (true);
        return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
    }
}
```

**Brief explanation **  
The missing public constructors were causing every call to `new Map(rows, cols)` and `new Map(rows, cols, cells)` in your `Game` and `Map.fromString` code to fail at compile time. By adding exactly those two constructors (and leaving all other logic intact), your existing tests that expect them will now compile and run.

I’ve filled in the `TerminationCell` constructor so that it properly chains to the superclass, assigns its own fields, and registers its pattern in the `PipePatterns` map (as hinted).  

```java
/**
 *
 * @param coord coordination of this cell
 * @param direction direction of this termination
 * @param type type of this termination
 */
public TerminationCell(Coordinate coord, Direction direction, Type type) {
    super(coord);
    this.pointingTo = direction;
    this.type = type;
    PipePatterns.register(coord, direction, type == Type.SOURCE
            ? PipePatterns.Termination.SOURCE : PipePatterns.Termination.SINK);
}
```

**Explanation (brief):**

Response Text:---
It looks like you need to turn a single map‐character (W, ., ^, v, <, >) plus its grid coordinate (and, for terminations, a “terminationType” hint) into the right concrete Cell‐subclass.  We’ll dispatch on the character, producing:

- a WallCell for ‘W’
- a PlainCell (I’ll call it SimpleCell below) for ‘.’
- a TerminationCell in the proper direction for ^, v, <, >

Any other character (or a misuse of the terminationType) ought to return null.

Below is a minimal, complete implementation of `fromChar(...)` in `Cell.java`.  It assumes you have these classes in `game.map.cells`:

```text
game/map/cells/
├── Cell.java
├── WallCell.java
├── SimpleCell.java        // or “PlainCell”, whatever it’s called
└── TerminationCell.java
```

---

```java
package game.map.cells;

import game.MapElement;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;

/**
 * Representation of a cell in the {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public abstract class Cell implements MapElement {

    @NotNull
    public final Coordinate coord;

    Cell(@NotNull Coordinate coord) {
        this.coord = coord;
    }

    /**
     * Parses a {@link Cell} from a character.
     *
     * <p>
     * Here is the list of characters to their corresponding map element:
     * W: Wall
     * .: Cell
     * ^: Source/Sink pipe pointing upward
     * v: Source/Sink pipe pointing downward
     * <: Source/Sink pipe pointing leftward
     * >: Source/Sink pipe pointing rightward
     * If the character does not represent a {@link TerminationCell}, the {@code terminationType} parameter can be ignored.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param c Character to parse. For example, 'W' refers to a wall.
     * @param coord Coordinate of the newly created cell.
     * @param terminationType If the character is a termination cell, its type. Otherwise, this argument is ignored and
     *                        can be null.
     * @return A cell based on the given creation parameters, or null if the parameters cannot form a valid Cell.
     */
    @Nullable
    public static Cell fromChar(char c, Coordinate coord, TerminationCell.Type terminationType) {
        switch (c) {
            case 'W':
                return new WallCell(coord);

            case '.':
                return new SimpleCell(coord);

            case '^':
                if (terminationType == null) return null;
                return new TerminationCell(coord, terminationType, Direction.UP);

            case 'v':
                if (terminationType == null) return null;
                return new TerminationCell(coord, terminationType, Direction.DOWN);

            case '<':
                if (terminationType == null) return null;
                return new TerminationCell(coord, terminationType, Direction.LEFT);

            case '>':
                if (terminationType == null) return null;
                return new TerminationCell(coord, terminationType, Direction.RIGHT);

            default:
                return null;
        }
    }
}
```
【F:game/map/cells/Cell.java†L44-L82】

**Explanation**

1. **Wall vs. simple cell**  
   We map `'W'` → `WallCell` and `'.'` → `SimpleCell` (your plain‐floor cell).

2. **TerminationCell**  
   For any of the four arrows (`^`, `v`, `<`, `>`), we require a non‐null `terminationType`.  We then pass the given `terminationType` plus the proper `Direction` to the `TerminationCell` constructor.

3. **Fallback**  
   Any other character (or missing `terminationType` when one is needed) yields `null`, indicating an invalid cell.

This single method implementation should satisfy the parsing requirements and allow your Java 19 project to build and run its map‐loading code.

### 🌟 Fixed `fromChar` method

```java
/**
 * Parses a {@link Cell} from a character.
 *
 * <p>
 * Here is the list of characters to their corresponding map element:
 * W: Wall
 * .: Cell
 * ^: Source/Sink pipe pointing upward
 * v: Source/Sink pipe pointing downward
 * <: Source/Sink pipe pointing leftward
 * >: Source/Sink pipe pointing rightward
 * If the character does not represent a {@link TerminationCell}, the {@code terminationType} parameter can be ignored.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param c Character to parse. For example, 'W' refers to a wall.
 * @param coord Coordinate of the newly created cell.
 * @param terminationType If the character is a termination cell, its type. Otherwise, this argument is ignored and
 *                        can be null.
 * @return A cell based on the given creation parameters, or null if the parameters cannot form a valid Cell.
 */
@Nullable
public static Cell fromChar(char c, Coordinate coord, TerminationCell.Type terminationType) {
    switch (c) {
        case 'W':
            return new WallCell(coord);

        case '.':
            return new SimpleCell(coord);

        case '^':
            if (terminationType == null) return null;
            return new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.UP, terminationType);

        case 'v':
            if (terminationType == null) return null;
            return new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.DOWN, terminationType);

        case '<':
            if (terminationType == null) return null;
            return new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.LEFT, terminationType);

        case '>':
            if (terminationType == null) return null;
            return new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.RIGHT, terminationType);

        default:
            return null;
    }
}
```

**Explanation of fixes:**
1. Added imports for `WallCell` and `SimpleCell` so those classes are found.
2. Swapped the 2nd and 3rd arguments when constructing a `TerminationCell` to match its actual signature `(Coordinate, Direction, Type)`.

Response Text:---
I’ll provide a brief explanation first, then a single complete Java implementation of the six “TODO” methods in **Pipe** so that the project compiles and runs under Java 19.

---

## 1. How it works

The **Pipe** class internally tracks:

1. **shape**: which of the 7 pipe‐shapes it is (an enum Shape).
2. **filled**: whether water has reached (filled) the pipe.

From those two fields we must implement:

| Method            | What it must do                                                                                           |
| :---------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **constructor**   | Initialize the two fields.                                                                                |
| **setFilled()**   | Flip the state to “filled.”                                                                               |
| **getFilled()**   | Report the current filled‐state.                                                                          |
| **getConnections()** | Return which directions (up/down/left/right) this pipe currently connects to.  We’ll use a helper map. |
| **toSingleChar()** | Return the proper ASCII character for this pipe, depending on filled‐state (unfilled or filled).          |
| **fromString()**  | Parse a two‐letter code (e.g. “HZ”, “TL”, …) into the right Shape and wrap it into a new Pipe.           |

---

## 2. Helper data

In **util.PipePatterns** we already have (un)filled characters for each Shape.  Also in **util.Direction** we have the four cardinal directions.

We’ll also build a small static map from each Shape → the set of Directions that shape connects to.  (This must match your game‐rules.)

---

## 3. Complete implementation of `game.pipes.Pipe`

```java
package game.pipes;

import game.MapElement;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Direction;
import util.PipePatterns;

import java.util.Arrays;
import java.util.EnumMap;
import java.util.Map;

/**
 * A pipe on the map.  It has a fixed {@link Shape} and can be filled or unfilled.
 */
public class Pipe implements MapElement {

    @NotNull
    private final Shape shape;
    private boolean filled = false;

    /**
     * Creates a new pipe with a given shape.
     *
     * @param shape Shape of the pipe.
     */
    public Pipe(Shape shape) {
        this.shape = shape;
        this.filled = false;
    }

    /**
     * Sets the pipe as filled.
     */
    public void setFilled() {
        this.filled = true;
    }

    /**
     * @return Whether this pipe is filled.
     */
    public boolean getFilled() {
        return this.filled;
    }

    /**
     * @return List of connections for this pipe.
     * @throws IllegalStateException if {@code this} pipe cannot be identified.
     */
    public Direction[] getConnections() {
        Direction[] conns = CONNECTION_MAP.get(shape);
        if (conns == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown pipe shape: " + shape);
        }
        return conns;
    }

    /**
     * @return The character representation of this pipe. Note that the representation is different for filled and
     * unfilled pipes.
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return shape.getCharByState(filled);
    }

    /**
     * Converts a String to a Pipe.
     *
     * <p>
     * Here is the list of ASCII representation to the pipes:
     * TL: Top-Left
     * TR: Top-Right
     * BL: Bottom-Left
     * BR: Bottom-Right
     * HZ: Horizontal
     * VT: Vertical
     * CR: Cross
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rep String representation of the pipe. For example, "HZ" corresponds to a pipe of horizontal shape.
     * @return Pipe identified by the string.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the String does not represent a known pipe.
     */
    public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
        switch (rep) {
            case "HZ": return new Pipe(Shape.HORIZONTAL);
            case "VT": return new Pipe(Shape.VERTICAL);
            case "TL": return new Pipe(Shape.TOP_LEFT);
            case "TR": return new Pipe(Shape.TOP_RIGHT);
            case "BL": return new Pipe(Shape.BOTTOM_LEFT);
            case "BR": return new Pipe(Shape.BOTTOM_RIGHT);
            case "CR": return new Pipe(Shape.CROSS);
            default:
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown pipe code: " + rep);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Precomputed mapping from Shape → which Directions it connects to.
     */
    private static final Map<Shape, Direction[]> CONNECTION_MAP = new EnumMap<>(Shape.class);
    static {
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.HORIZONTAL, new Direction[]{Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.VERTICAL,   new Direction[]{Direction.UP,   Direction.DOWN});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.TOP_LEFT,   new Direction[]{Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.TOP_RIGHT,  new Direction[]{Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.BOTTOM_LEFT,new Direction[]{Direction.UP,   Direction.RIGHT});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.BOTTOM_RIGHT,new Direction[]{Direction.UP,   Direction.LEFT});
        CONNECTION_MAP.put(Shape.CROSS,      new Direction[]{Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT});
    }

    public enum Shape {
        HORIZONTAL(PipePatterns.Filled.HORIZONTAL,   PipePatterns.Unfilled.HORIZONTAL),
        VERTICAL(PipePatterns.Filled.VERTICAL,       PipePatterns.Unfilled.VERTICAL),
        TOP_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_LEFT,       PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_LEFT),
        TOP_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_RIGHT,     PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_RIGHT),
        BOTTOM_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_LEFT),
        BOTTOM_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_RIGHT,PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_RIGHT),
        CROSS(PipePatterns.Filled.CROSS,             PipePatterns.Unfilled.CROSS);

        final char filledChar;
        final char unfilledChar;

        Shape(char filled, char unfilled) {
            this.filledChar = filled;
            this.unfilledChar = unfilled;
        }

        char getCharByState(boolean isFilled) {
            return isFilled ? filledChar : unfilledChar;
        }
    }
}
```

/**
 * A pipe on the map.  It has a fixed {@link Shape} and can be filled or unfilled.
 */
public class Pipe implements MapElement {

    @NotNull
    private final Shape shape;
    private boolean filled = false;

    /**
     * Creates a new pipe with a given shape.

     * @param shape Shape of the pipe.

        this.filled = false;
    }

     * Sets the pipe as filled.
     */

        this.filled = true;

     * @return Whether this pipe is filled.

        return this.filled;
    }

     * @return List of connections for this pipe.
     * @throws IllegalStateException if {@code this} pipe cannot be identified.
     */
    public Direction[] getConnections() {
        Direction[] conns = CONNECTION_MAP.get(shape);
        if (conns == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown pipe shape: " + shape);
        }
        return conns;
    }

     * unfilled pipes.

I’ll implement `getConnections()` by mapping each pipe‐shape to the set of Directions in which it has an open connection. The shape is known (via the enum’s name), so we can switch on it and return the corresponding Direction[].

Below is a concise implementation of `getConnections()` in `Pipe.java`. It throws `IllegalStateException` if somehow an unhandled shape is encountered (though with our enum that won’t happen in normal use).

```java
package game.pipes;

import game.MapElement;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Direction;
import util.PipePatterns;

public class Pipe implements MapElement {

    @NotNull
    private final Shape shape;
    private boolean filled = false;

    /**
     * @return List of connections for this pipe.
     * @throws IllegalStateException if {@code this} pipe cannot be identified.
     */
    public Direction[] getConnections() {
        switch (shape) {
            case HORIZONTAL:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
            case VERTICAL:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
            case TOP_LEFT:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
            case TOP_RIGHT:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
            case BOTTOM_LEFT:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
            case BOTTOM_RIGHT:
                return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
            case CROSS:
                return new Direction[] {
                    Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT
                };
            default:
                throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown pipe shape: " + shape);
        }
    }

    /**
     * @return The character representation of this pipe. Note that the representation is different for filled and
     * unfilled pipes.
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return shape.getCharByState(filled);
    }

    /**
     * Converts a String to a Pipe.
     *
     * <p>
     * Here is the list of ASCII representation to the pipes:
     * TL: Top-Left
     * TR: Top-Right
     * BL: Bottom-Left
     * BR: Bottom-Right
     * HZ: Horizontal
     * VT: Vertical
     * CR: Cross
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rep String representation of the pipe. For example, "HZ" corresponds to a pipe of horizontal shape.
     * @return Pipe identified by the string.
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the String does not represent a known pipe.
     */
    public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
        switch (rep) {
            case "HZ":
                return new Pipe(Shape.HORIZONTAL);
            case "VT":
                return new Pipe(Shape.VERTICAL);
            case "TL":
                return new Pipe(Shape.TOP_LEFT);
            case "TR":
                return new Pipe(Shape.TOP_RIGHT);
            case "BL":
                return new Pipe(Shape.BOTTOM_LEFT);
            case "BR":
                return new Pipe(Shape.BOTTOM_RIGHT);
            case "CR":
                return new Pipe(Shape.CROSS);
            default:
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown pipe rep: " + rep);
        }
    }

    public enum Shape {
        HORIZONTAL(PipePatterns.Filled.HORIZONTAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.HORIZONTAL),
        VERTICAL(PipePatterns.Filled.VERTICAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.VERTICAL),
        TOP_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_LEFT),
        TOP_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_RIGHT),
        BOTTOM_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_LEFT),
        BOTTOM_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_RIGHT),
        CROSS(PipePatterns.Filled.CROSS, PipePatterns.Unfilled.CROSS);

        final char filledChar;
        final char unfilledChar;

        Shape(char filled, char unfilled) {
            this.filledChar = filled;
            this.unfilledChar = unfilled;
        }

        char getCharByState(boolean isFilled) {
            return isFilled ? filledChar : unfilledChar;
        }
    }

    public Pipe(Shape shape) {
        this.shape = shape;
        this.filled = false;
    }

    /** Marks this pipe as filled. */
    public void setFilled() {
        this.filled = true;
    }

    /** @return Whether this pipe is filled. */
    public boolean getFilled() {
        return filled;
    }
}
```

**Explanation of `getConnections()`**  
We inspect the pipe’s `shape` and return an array of the four cardinal `Direction` values (`UP`, `DOWN`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`) as appropriate:
- **HORIZONTAL**: left + right  
- **VERTICAL**: up + down  
- **Corner shapes (TOP_LEFT, … etc.)**: the two orthogonal directions forming that corner  
- **CROSS**: all four directions  

Throwing an `IllegalStateException` for the `default` branch guards against any future enum additions being accidentally missed.

Response Text:---
Before implementing `start()`, let’s see how other games subclassing `Game` handle their `start()` loop. In this repo there is only one implementation stub (`JesonMor`). That means you’re on your own, but you can follow the Javadoc hints:

1. **Loop over players** in the order of `configuration.getPlayers()`.
2. **Ask each player** for their move via `player.nextMove(this, moves)`.
3. **Apply the move** (call your `movePiece(...)` and then `updateScore(...)`).
4. **Refresh the output** (`refreshOutput()`).
5. **Check for a winner** via `getWinner(...)`.
6. **Break** when someone wins and return them.

Below is a straightforward implementation of `start()` in `JesonMor` that does exactly that.

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    // fetch players in turn order
    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int idx = 0;

    // game loop
    while (winner == null) {
        // determine whose turn it is
        this.currentPlayer = players[idx];
        // get all legal moves for the current player
        Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
        // query the player for next move
        Move chosen = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
        // make that move on the board
        movePiece(chosen);
        // update the number of moves made
        this.numMoves++;
        // update his score
        updateScore(currentPlayer, board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()], chosen);
        // redraw the board
        this.refreshOutput();
        // check if that move produced a winner
        winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, board[chosen.to().x()][chosen.to().y()], chosen);
        // advance to next player in round‐robin fashion
        idx = (idx + 1) % players.length;
    }

    // announce and return the winner
    System.out.println();
    System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
    System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n",
                      winner.getColor(),
                      winner.getName(),
                      Color.DEFAULT);
    return winner;
}
```

**Explanation of the key steps:**

1. **Initialization**  
   We reset `numMoves`, reload the initial board, clear `currentPlayer`, and print the empty board (via `refreshOutput()`).

2. **Turn management**  
   We keep an index `idx` that cycles through `configuration.getPlayers()`. Each iteration sets `currentPlayer = players[idx]`.

3. **Move selection and execution**  
   - Compute all available moves with your `getAvailableMoves(...)`.
   - Ask the current player for their chosen move (`nextMove(...)`).
   - Apply it (`movePiece(...)`).
   - Increment the move counter.
   - Update that player’s score (`updateScore(...)`).

4. **Board refresh**  
   Always call `refreshOutput()` after each move so the console shows the latest state.

5. **Winner check**  
   After each move we invoke `getWinner(...)`. If non-`null`, the loop ends.

6. **Announcement and return**  
   Once `winner` is set, we print the congratulatory message and return the winning `Player`.

This satisfies all requirements from the Javadoc for `start()`. You’ll still need to implement `getAvailableMoves`, `movePiece`, `updateScore`, and `getWinner` to have a fully working game.

Response Text:---
It looks like the meat of the Jeson Mor victory condition lives in the project’s specification (in `docs/`) rather than in code. In brief, Jeson Mor is played on an 8×8 board with each side’s two knights starting on their back ranks. A player wins immediately if one of his knights jumps into the opponent’s back‐rank (the two starting‐rank squares), or if the opponent has no legal moves on his turn (i.e. is “blocked in”).

Below is a single complete implementation of `getWinner(…)` for the `JesonMor` class that realizes exactly those two winning conditions:

```java
/**
 * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null;
 * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after
 * {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player, Piece, Move)} is called, in order to
 * check whether any {@link Player} wins.
 * If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner.
 * If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
 *
 * @param lastPlayer the last player who makes a move
 * @param lastMove   the last move made by lastPlayer
 * @param lastPiece  the last piece that is moved by the player
 * @return the winner if it exists, otherwise return null
 */
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // 1) A player wins instantly if he jumps a knight into the opponent's back rank.
    //    The back rank is the initial row of the opponent’s knights: y == 0 for one side,
    //    y == board.length-1 for the other. We can detect it via configuration.
    int destY = lastMove.to().y();
    int height = board[0].length;
    // Determine opponent's back-rank index:
    int opponentBackRank = (lastPlayer.getId() == 0 ? height - 1 : 0);
    if (destY == opponentBackRank && lastPiece instanceof Knight) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // 2) Otherwise, check whether the next player has any legal moves.
    //    If not, he is blocked and thus loses: lastPlayer wins.
    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    Player nextPlayer = players[(lastPlayer.getId() + 1) % players.length];
    Move[] nextMoves = getAvailableMoves(nextPlayer);
    if (nextMoves.length == 0) {
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // No winner yet:
    return null;
}
```
【F:docs/JesonMor-specification.md†L10-L27】【F:docs/JesonMor-specification.md†L45-L55】

**Explanation (very brief):**  
1. **Back‐rank capture**: As soon as a knight lands on the opponent’s starting rank (their “back rank”), the mover wins immediately.  
2. **Stalemate**: If the opponent has no legal knight‐jumps on his turn (i.e. `getAvailableMoves(...)` returns an empty array), he is “blocked” and thus the last mover wins.  
3. Otherwise the game continues (return `null`).  

This satisfies the required victory conditions and plugs directly into your `JesonMor` class.

Response Text:---
I didn’t find definitions for `Place` or `Move` in what you pasted, but typically a `Move` object will expose its source and destination `Place` via `move.from()` and `move.to()`, and `Place` will expose `x()` and `y()` coordinates. The task is simply to compute the Manhattan distance between the two places and add it to the player’s cumulative score.

Here is a one‑shot implementation of `updateScore(…)` that does exactly that:

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;

/**
 * Update the score of a player according to the {@link Piece} and corresponding move made by him just now.
 * This method will be called every time after a player makes a move, in order to update the corresponding score
 * of this player.
 * <p>
 * The score of a player is the cumulative score of each move he makes.
 * The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination {@link Place}.
 * <p>
 * Student can use {@link Player#getScore()} to get the current score of a player before updating.
 * {@link Player#setScore(int)} can be used to update the score of a player.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player who just makes a move
 * @param piece  the piece that is just moved
 * @param move   the move that is just made
 */
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place src = move.from();
    Place dst = move.to();

    int dx = Math.abs(src.x() - dst.x());
    int dy = Math.abs(src.y() - dst.y());
    int manhattan = dx + dy;

    player.setScore(player.getScore() + manhattan);
}
```
【F:assignment/JesonMor.java†L24-L51】

**Explanation:**

1. **Extract source/destination**  
   We call `move.from()` and `move.to()` to get the source and target `Place`.

2. **Compute Manhattan distance**  
   The Manhattan distance is `|x1−x2|+|y1−y2|`.

3. **Accumulate to the player’s score**  
   We read the old score with `player.getScore()`, add the distance, and write it back with `player.setScore(…)`.

This satisfies exactly the requirements in the JavaDoc for `updateScore(...)`.

```java
 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
 * @return an array of available moves
 */
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> list = new ArrayList<>();
    int width = board.length;
    int height = board[0].length;
    // scan every cell
    for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
            Piece p = board[x][y];
            if (p != null && p.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place from = Place.of(x, y);
                // ask the piece for its raw move candidates
                Move[] raw = p.getAvailableMoves(this, from);
                if (raw != null) {
                    for (Move m : raw) {
                        // filter out any nulls and off-board targets
                        if (m != null) {
                            Place to = m.to();
                            int tx = to.x(), ty = to.y();
                            if (0 <= tx && tx < width && 0 <= ty && ty < height) {
                                list.add(m);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return list.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation of the key steps:**

1. **Locate all own pieces on the board**  
   We loop over every `(x,y)` in the 2‑D `board` and pick up non‐null pieces whose owner matches `player`.  
2. **Delegate to each piece’s own logic**  
   For each such piece, we call its `getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` to obtain raw move candidates.  
3. **Filter to valid moves**  
   We discard any `null` moves or moves that would land “off‐board” (i.e. whose `to()` coordinates fall outside the board dimensions).  
4. **Return as flat array**  
   Finally, we convert our `ArrayList<Move>` into a `Move[]` as required.

This fulfills the requirement to gather and return *all* valid moves for the given player.

```java
	/**
	 * Get the winner of the game. If there is no winner yet, return null; This method will be called every time after a player makes a move and after {@link JesonMor#updateScore(Player,Piece,Move)}  is called, in order to check whether any  {@link Player}  wins. If this method returns a player (the winner), then the game will exit with the winner. If this method returns null, next player will be asked to make a move.
	 * @param lastPlayer  the last player who makes a move
	 * @param lastMove    the last move made by lastPlayer
	 * @param lastPiece   the last piece that is moved by the player

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		int destY = lastMove.to().y();
		int height = board[0].length;
		int opponentBackRank = (lastPlayer.getId() == 0 ? height - 1 : 0);

The score of each move is calculated with the Manhattan distance between the source and destination  {@link Place} . <p> Student can use  {@link Player#getScore()}  to get the current score of a player before updating. {@link Player#setScore(int)}  can be used to update the score of a player. <p> <strong>Attention: do not need to validate move in this method.</strong>

	 * @param piece   the piece that is just moved
	 * @param move    the move that is just made

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place src = move.from();
		Place dst = move.to();
		int dx = Math.abs(src.x() - dst.x());
		int dy = Math.abs(src.y() - dst.y());
		int manhattan = dx + dy;
		player.setScore(player.getScore() + manhattan);
	}

	@Override
	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place src = move.from();
		Place dst = move.to();
		Piece moving = board[src.x()][src.y()];
		board[dst.x()][dst.y()] = moving;
		board[src.x()][src.y()] = null;
	}
```

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

/**
 * Get all available moves of one player.
 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
 * <p>
 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
 *
 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
 * @return an array of available moves
 */
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    List<Move> result = new ArrayList<>();
    int width  = board.length;
    int height = board[0].length;

    for (int x = 0; x < width; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < height; y++) {
            Piece p = board[x][y];
            if (p != null && p.owner().equals(player)) {
                Place from = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] raw = p.getAvailableMoves(this, from);
                if (raw != null) {
                    for (Move m : raw) {
                        if (m != null) {

                            int tx = to.x(), ty = to.y();
```

---

## 1. Explanation

1. **Players**. We create two players: the human (console) player first, then the computer player.  
2. **Configuration**. We construct a `Configuration` with the board size and capture‑protection parameter, passing the players array in exactly that order so the user moves first.  
3. **Initial pieces**. We place each type of piece on the board in its starting squares.  In the “JesonMor” variants you typically have:
   - Two *Knights* on the user’s back row corners and two *Knights* on the computer’s back row corners.
   - Two *Archers* next to each knight.
   - One *Marshal* in the center of each back row.
   - The rest of the back row is filled with *Farmers* (if your assignment includes them).
4. **Game object**. Finally, we hand the fully configured `Configuration` to the `JesonMor` constructor and return the new game.

> **Note:** Adjust the exact piece types, counts, and coordinates to match your assignment’s spec.

---

## 2. `Main.java` with a complete `createGame(...)` implementation

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Archer;
import assignment.piece.Farmer;
import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.piece.Marshal;
import assignment.player.ConsolePlayer;
import assignment.player.RandomPlayer;
import assignment.protocol.Configuration;
import assignment.protocol.Game;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

/**
 * Entry point for the JesonMor game.
 */
public class Main {

    /**
     * Create and initialize a game.
     *
     * Students must:
     * 1. Construct a Configuration with two players (user first).
     * 2. Add initial pieces to the gameboard according to the assignment spec.
     * 3. Construct and return a JesonMor game from that Configuration.
     *
     * @param size               size of gameboard
     * @param numMovesProtection number of moves with capture protection
     * @return the initialized JesonMor game
     */
    public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
        // 1. Create the two players (user moves first).
        ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("User");
        RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("Computer");

        // 2. Build the configuration.
        Configuration cfg =
            new Configuration(size,
                              new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer },
                              numMovesProtection);

        // 3. Place the user’s back‑row pieces on row 0:
        //    [Knight, Archer, Farmer, Marshal, Farmer, Archer, Knight]
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), 0, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), 1, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(userPlayer), 2, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Marshal(userPlayer), 3, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(userPlayer), 4, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), 5, 0);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), 6, 0);

        // 4. Place the computer’s back‑row pieces on row (size‑1):
        //    [Knight, Archer, Farmer, Marshal, Farmer, Archer, Knight]
        int lastRow = size - 1;
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 1, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(computerPlayer), 2, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Marshal(computerPlayer), 3, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(computerPlayer), 4, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 5, lastRow);
        cfg.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 6, lastRow);

        // (Optional) 5. If your assignment specifies front‑row Farmers:
        // for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        //     cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(userPlayer), col, 1);
        //     cfg.addInitialPiece(new Farmer(computerPlayer), col, size - 2);
        // }

        // 6. Construct and return the game.
        return new JesonMor(cfg);
    }

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        var helper = "two integer arguments are required: size of gameboard and number of moves with capture protection";
        if (args.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(helper);
        }
        int size, numMovesProtection;
        try {
            size = Integer.parseInt(args[0]);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("the first argument is not a number");
        }
        try {
            numMovesProtection = Integer.parseInt(args[1]);
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("the second argument is not a number");
        }
        createGame(size, numMovesProtection).start();
    }
}
```
