Response Text:---
**Explanation**

The compilation errors

```
The constructor GameState(GameBoard) is undefined
The constructor GameState(GameBoard, int) is undefined
```

are due to the fact that the two “constructors” in `GameState` were mistakenly declared with a return type (`void`) and thus became ordinary methods rather than constructors. In Java, constructors must not declare any return type. As a result, no real constructors existed, so calls like `new GameState(gameBoard)` or `new GameState(gameBoard, numLives)` could not resolve.

To fix this, simply remove the `void` return type on those methods so that they become proper constructors.

---

```java
package pa1.model;

import pa1.controller.GameBoardController;
import pa1.view.GameBoardView;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Class for tracking the state of multiple game components.
 */
public class GameState {

    /**
     * Number representing unlimited number of lives for a player.
     */
    public static final int UNLIMITED_LIVES = -1;

    /**
     * The game board managed by this instance.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    /**
     * {@link MoveStack} instance of all moves performed by the player.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final MoveStack moveStack = new MoveStack();

    /**
     * The number of deaths of the player.
     */
    private int numDeaths = 0;

    /**
     * The number of moves performed by the player (excluding invalid moves).
     */
    private int numMoves = 0;

    /**
     * The number of lives the player has.
     */
    private int numLives;

    /**
     * The number of gems initially on the game board when this instance was created.
     */
    private final int initialNumOfGems;

    /**
     * @return The instance of the managed {@link MoveStack}.
     */
    @NotNull
    public MoveStack getMoveStack() {
        return moveStack;
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance. <p> The player will have an unlimited number of lives by default. </p>
     * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance. <p> Note: Do NOT throw an exception when {@code numLives} is zero. This will be used in our testing. </p>
     * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
     * @param numLives   Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull final GameBoard gameBoard, final int numLives) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        if (numLives < 0) {
            this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        } else {
            this.numLives = numLives;
        }
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    // … rest of class unchanged …
    
    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been won. <p> The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board. </p>
     * @return  Whether the player has won the game.
     */
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems() == 0;
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been lost. <p> The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this condition should never trigger. </p>
     * @return  Whether the player has lost the game.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
            return false;
        }
        return numLives <= 0;
    }

    /**
     * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     * @param delta  The number of lives to give the player.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives += delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decreases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     * @param delta  The number of lives to take from the player.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives -= delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decrementNumLives() {
        return decreaseNumLives(1);
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
     * @return  The new number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumMoves() {
        return ++numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
     * @return  The new number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumDeaths() {
        return ++numDeaths;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The current number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int getNumDeaths() {
        return numDeaths;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The current number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * @return  Whether the player has unlimited lives.
     */
    public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
        return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int getNumLives() {
        return hasUnlimitedLives() ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The number of gems that is still present on the game board.
     */
    public int getNumGems() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * <p> At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula: </p> <ul> <li>The initial score of any game board is {@code gameBoardSize}.</li> <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li> <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li> <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li> <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li> </ul>
     * @return  The current score of this game.
     */
    public int getScore() {
        int boardSize    = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
        int gemsScore    = gameBoard.getNumGems() * 10;
        int movePenalty  = numMoves;
        int undoPenalty  = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
        int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
        return boardSize + gemsScore - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
    }

    /**
     * @return  A controller of the managed game board for mutation.
     */
    public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
        return new GameBoardController(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * @return  A read-only view of the managed game board.
     */
    public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
        return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * @return  The instance of the managed {@link GameBoard}.
     */
    @NotNull
    public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
        return gameBoard;
    }
}
```

```java
package pa1.model;

import pa1.controller.GameBoardController;
import pa1.view.GameBoardView;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Class for tracking the state of multiple game components.
 */
public class GameState {

	/**
	 * Number representing unlimited number of lives for a player.
	 */
	public static final int UNLIMITED_LIVES = -1;

	/**
	 * The game board managed by this instance.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final GameBoard gameBoard;

	/**
	 * {@link MoveStack} instance of all moves performed by the player.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final MoveStack moveStack = new MoveStack();

	/**
	 * The number of deaths of the player.
	 */
	private int numDeaths = 0;

	/**
	 * The number of moves performed by the player (excluding invalid moves).
	 */
	private int numMoves = 0;

	/**
	 * The number of lives the player has.
	 */
	private int numLives;

	/**
	 * The number of gems initially on the game board when this instance was created.
	 */
	private final int initialNumOfGems;

	/**
	 * @return The instance of the managed {@link MoveStack}.
	 */
	public MoveStack getMoveStack() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance. <p> The player will have an unlimited number of lives by default. </p>
	 * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
	 */
	public void GameState(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance. <p> Note: Do NOT throw an exception when  {@code  numLives}  is zero. This will be used in our testing. </p>
	 * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
	 * @param numLives   Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
	 */
	public void GameState(final GameBoard gameBoard, final int numLives) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		if (numLives < 0) {
			this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		} else {
			this.numLives = numLives;
		}
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been won. <p> The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has won the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return gameBoard.getNumGems() == 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been lost. <p> The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this condition should never trigger. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has lost the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return false;
		}
		return numLives <= 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
	 * @param delta  The number of lives to give the player.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives += delta;
		return numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * Decreases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
	 * @param delta  The number of lives to take from the player.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives -= delta;
		return numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int decrementNumLives() {
		return decreaseNumLives(1);
	}

	/**
	 * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
	 * @return  The new number of moves taken by the player.
	 */
	public int incrementNumMoves() {
		return ++numMoves;
	}

	/**
	 * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
	 * @return  The new number of deaths of the player.
	 */
	public int incrementNumDeaths() {
		return ++numDeaths;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The current number of deaths of the player.
	 */
	public int getNumDeaths() {
		return numDeaths;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The current number of moves taken by the player.
	 */
	public int getNumMoves() {
		return numMoves;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether the player has unlimited lives.
	 */
	public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
		return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int getNumLives() {
		return hasUnlimitedLives() ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of gems that is still present on the game board.
	 */
	public int getNumGems() {
		return gameBoard.getNumGems();
	}

	/**
	 * <p> At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula: </p> <ul> <li>The initial score of any game board is  {@code  gameBoardSize} .</li> <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li> <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li> <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li> <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li> </ul>
	 * @return  The current score of this game.
	 */
	public int getScore() {
		int boardSize = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
		int gemsScore = gameBoard.getNumGems() * 10;
		int movePenalty = numMoves;
		int undoPenalty = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
		int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
		return boardSize + gemsScore - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  A controller of the managed game board for mutation.
	 */
	public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
		return new GameBoardController(this.gameBoard);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  A read-only view of the managed game board.
	 */
	public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
		return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The instance of the managed  {@link GameBoard} .
	 */
	@NotNull
	public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
		return gameBoard;
	}
}
```

package pa1.model;

import pa1.controller.GameBoardController;
import pa1.view.GameBoardView;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Class for tracking the state of multiple game components.
 */
public class GameState {

    /**
     * Number representing unlimited number of lives for a player.
     */
    public static final int UNLIMITED_LIVES = -1;

    /**
     * The game board managed by this instance.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    /**
     * {@link MoveStack} instance of all moves performed by the player.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final MoveStack moveStack = new MoveStack();

    /**
     * The number of deaths of the player.
     */
    private int numDeaths = 0;

    /**
     * The number of moves performed by the player (excluding invalid moves).
     */
    private int numMoves = 0;

    /**
     * The number of lives the player has.
     */
    private int numLives;

    /**
     * The number of gems initially on the game board when this instance was created.
     */
    private final int initialNumOfGems;

    /**
     * @return The instance of the managed {@link MoveStack}.
     */
    @NotNull
    public MoveStack getMoveStack() {
        return moveStack;
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance. <p> The player will have an unlimited number of lives by default. </p>
     * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull final GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance. <p> Note: Do NOT throw an exception when {@code numLives} is zero. This will be used in our testing. </p>
     * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
     * @param numLives   Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull final GameBoard gameBoard, final int numLives) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        if (numLives < 0) {
            this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        } else {
            this.numLives = numLives;
        }
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    // … rest of class unchanged …
    
    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been won. <p> The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board. </p>
     * @return  Whether the player has won the game.
     */
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems() == 0;
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been lost. <p> The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this condition should never trigger. </p>
     * @return  Whether the player has lost the game.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
            return false;
        }
        return numLives <= 0;
    }

    /**
     * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     * @param delta  The number of lives to give the player.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives += delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decreases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     * @param delta  The number of lives to take from the player.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives -= delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
     * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decrementNumLives() {
        return decreaseNumLives(1);
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
     * @return  The new number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumMoves() {
        return ++numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
     * @return  The new number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumDeaths() {
        return ++numDeaths;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The current number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int getNumDeaths() {
        return numDeaths;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The current number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * @return  Whether the player has unlimited lives.
     */
    public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
        return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int getNumLives() {
        return hasUnlimitedLives() ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
    }

    /**
     * @return  The number of gems that is still present on the game board.
     */
    public int getNumGems() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * <p> At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula: </p> <ul> <li>The initial score of any game board is {@code gameBoardSize}.</li> <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li> <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li> <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li> <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li> </ul>
     * @return  The current score of this game.
     */
    public int getScore() {
        int boardSize    = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
        int gemsScore    = gameBoard.getNumGems() * 10;
        int movePenalty  = numMoves;
        int undoPenalty  = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
        int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
        return boardSize + gemsScore - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
    }

    /**
     * @return  A controller of the managed game board for mutation.
     */
    public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
        return new GameBoardController(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * @return  A read-only view of the managed game board.
     */
    public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
        return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /**
     * @return  The instance of the managed {@link GameBoard}.
     */
    @NotNull
    public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
        return gameBoard;
    }
}

Response Text:---
It turns out the two “constructors” in your `GameState.java` aren’t constructors at all but methods (they declare a return type `void`), so the compiler never actually defines `GameState(GameBoard)` or `GameState(GameBoard,int)` and all of your tests (and serializer) fail to find them.

You simply need to remove the “`void`” from those declarations so that they become real constructors. Below is the one‐and‐only corrected `GameState` class.

```java
package pa1.model;

import pa1.controller.GameBoardController;
import pa1.view.GameBoardView;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * Class for tracking the state of multiple game components.
 */
public class GameState {

    /**
     * Number representing unlimited number of lives for a player.
     */
    public static final int UNLIMITED_LIVES = -1;

    /**
     * The game board managed by this instance.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final GameBoard gameBoard;

    /**
     * {@link MoveStack} instance of all moves performed by the player.
     */
    @NotNull
    private final MoveStack moveStack = new MoveStack();

    /**
     * The number of deaths of the player.
     */
    private int numDeaths = 0;

    /**
     * The number of moves performed by the player (excluding invalid moves).
     */
    private int numMoves = 0;

    /**
     * The number of lives the player has.
     */
    private int numLives;

    /**
     * The number of gems initially on the game board when this instance was created.
     */
    private final int initialNumOfGems;

    /**
     * @return The instance of the managed {@link MoveStack}.
     */
    @NotNull
    public MoveStack getMoveStack() {
        return moveStack;
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance. 
     * <p>The player will have an unlimited number of lives by default.</p>
     *
     * @param gameBoard The game board to be managed by this instance.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull GameBoard gameBoard) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance.
     * <p>Note: Do NOT throw an exception when {@code numLives} is zero. This will be used in our testing.</p>
     *
     * @param gameBoard The game board to be managed by this instance.
     * @param numLives  Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull GameBoard gameBoard, int numLives) {
        this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
        if (numLives < 0) {
            this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
        } else {
            this.numLives = numLives;
        }
        this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    // … all other methods unchanged …

    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been won.
     * <p>The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board.</p>
     *
     * @return Whether the player has won the game.
     */
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems() == 0;
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game has been lost.
     * <p>The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives,
     * this condition should never trigger.</p>
     *
     * @return Whether the player has lost the game.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
            return false;
        }
        return numLives <= 0;
    }

    /**
     * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     *
     * @param delta The number of lives to give the player.
     * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int increaseNumLives(int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives += delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decreases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
     *
     * @param delta The number of lives to take from the player.
     * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decreaseNumLives(int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives -= delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
     *
     * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decrementNumLives() {
        return decreaseNumLives(1);
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
     *
     * @return The new number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumMoves() {
        return ++numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
     *
     * @return The new number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumDeaths() {
        return ++numDeaths;
    }

    /** @return The current number of deaths of the player. */
    public int getNumDeaths() {
        return numDeaths;
    }

    /** @return The current number of moves taken by the player. */
    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    /** @return Whether the player has unlimited lives. */
    public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
        return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int getNumLives() {
        return hasUnlimitedLives() ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
    }

    /** @return The number of gems still present on the game board. */
    public int getNumGems() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * <p>At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula:</p>
     * <ul>
     *   <li>The initial score of any game board is {@code gameBoardSize}.</li>
     *   <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li>
     *   <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li>
     *   <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li>
     *   <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li>
     * </ul>
     *
     * @return The current score of this game.
     */
    public int getScore() {
        int boardSize    = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
        int gemsScore    = gameBoard.getNumGems() * 10;
        int movePenalty  = numMoves;
        int undoPenalty  = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
        int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
        return boardSize + gemsScore - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
    }

    /** @return A controller of the managed game board for mutation. */
    public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
        return new GameBoardController(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /** @return A read-only view of the managed game board. */
    public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
        return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /** @return The instance of the managed {@link GameBoard}. */
    @NotNull
    public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
        return gameBoard;
    }
}
```
【F:pa1/model/GameState.java†L28-L52】【F:pa1/model/GameState.java†L53-L79】

**Explanation.**  
In Java, a constructor must omit any return type. The original code mistakenly declared them as:
```java
public void GameState(…){…}
```
which defines a *method* called `GameState`, not a constructor. Removing `void` makes them true constructors, satisfying all your test cases and serializers.

     * @param delta The number of lives to take from the player.
     * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decreaseNumLives(int delta) {
        if (hasUnlimitedLives()) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }
        numLives -= delta;
        return numLives;
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
     *
     * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int decrementNumLives() {
        return decreaseNumLives(1);
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
     *
     * @return The new number of moves taken by the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumMoves() {
        return ++numMoves;
    }

    /**
     * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
     *
     * @return The new number of deaths of the player.
     */
    public int incrementNumDeaths() {
        return ++numDeaths;
    }

    /** @return The current number of deaths of the player. */
    public int getNumDeaths() {
        return numDeaths;
    }

    /** @return The current number of moves taken by the player. */
    public int getNumMoves() {
        return numMoves;
    }

    /** @return Whether the player has unlimited lives. */
    public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
        return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives,
     * returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
     */
    public int getNumLives() {
        return hasUnlimitedLives() ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
    }

    public int getNumGems() {
        return gameBoard.getNumGems();
    }

    /**
     * <p>At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula:</p>
     * <ul>
     *   <li>The initial score of any game board is {@code gameBoardSize}.</li>
     *   <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li>
     *   <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li>
     *   <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li>
     *   <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li>
     * </ul>
     *
     * @return The current score of this game.
     */
    public int getScore() {
        int boardSize    = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
        int gemsScore    = gameBoard.getNumGems() * 10;
        int movePenalty  = numMoves;
        int undoPenalty  = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
        int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
        return boardSize + gemsScore - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
    }

    /** @return A controller of the managed game board for mutation. */
    public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
        return new GameBoardController(this.gameBoard);
    }

    /** @return A read-only view of the managed game board. */
    public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
        return new GameBoardView(this.gameBoard);
    }

    @NotNull
    public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
        return gameBoard;
    }

I’ll implement the `GameMap.parse(String mapText)` method so that it

1. Reads and validates the undo‐limit.
2. Parses each map line to build walls, empties, box destinations, players and boxes.
3. Enforces the constraints on players and boxes (unique uppercase‐players, matching box/player counts, etc.).
4. Returns a fully populated `GameMap`.

---

**Explanation (brief)**  
The implementation splits the input on line breaks, parses the first line as the undo limit (checking that it is ≥ −1), then iterates over the remaining lines, character by character, building up the coordinate‐to‐`Entity` map and the set of destination positions. It tracks seen players and boxes to enforce the one‐to‐one correspondence rules (unique uppercase letters for players; equal numbers of boxes and destinations; every box’s lowercase letter has a matching uppercase player and vice versa). Finally it constructs and returns a new `GameMap` instance.

---

```java
public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
    Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
    String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
    if (lines.length < 2) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
    }

    // 1) Parse undo limit
    int undoLimit;
    try {
        undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
    } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
    }
    if (undoLimit < -1) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
    }

    // 2) Prepare containers
    Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
    Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
    Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
    Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();

    // 3) Parse each map cell
    for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
        String row = lines[y];
        for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
            char c = row.charAt(x);
            Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
            switch (c) {
                case '#':
                    map.put(pos, new Wall());
                    break;
                case '.':
                    map.put(pos, new Empty());
                    break;
                case '@':
                    map.put(pos, new Empty());
                    destinations.add(pos);
                    break;
                default:
                    if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                        if (players.containsKey(c)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                        }
                        players.put(c, pos);
                        map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
                    } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                        if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
                        }
                        boxes.put(c, pos);
                        map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
                    } else {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    // 4) Validate player/box presence
    if (players.isEmpty()) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
    }
    if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
                + ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
    }

    // 5) Check box/player correspondence
    for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
        char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
        if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
        }
    }
    for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
        char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
        if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
        }
    }

    // 6) Build and return GameMap
    return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
}
```

    }

    // 2) Prepare containers
    Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
    Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
    Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
    Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();

    // 3) Parse each map cell
    for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
        String row = lines[y];
        for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
            char c = row.charAt(x);
            Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
            switch (c) {
                case '#':
                    map.put(pos, new Wall());
                    break;
                case '.':
                    map.put(pos, new Empty());
                    break;
                case '@':
                    map.put(pos, new Empty());
                    destinations.add(pos);
                    break;
                default:
                    if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                        if (players.containsKey(c)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                        }
                        players.put(c, pos);
                        map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
                    } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                        if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
                        }
                        boxes.put(c, pos);
                        map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
                    } else {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
                    }
            }
        }
    }

    // 4) Validate player/box presence
    if (players.isEmpty()) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
    }
    if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
                + ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
    }

    // 5) Check box/player correspondence
    for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
        char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
        if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
        }
    }
    for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
        char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
        if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
        }
    }

    // 6) Build and return GameMap
    return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
}

It looks like `getEntity(Position)` is currently unimplemented, so any code that wants to query “what is at (x,y)?” on the map will fail.  The intended behavior is simply to return whichever Entity was stored at that Position (or an `Empty` if nothing was ever put there).

Below is a completed `getEntity` method for `GameMap` that:

1. Null‑checks its argument.
2. Returns the mapped Entity if present.
3. Otherwise returns a fresh `Empty()` instance.

```java
/**
 * Get the entity object at the given position.
 *
 * @param position the position of the entity in the game map.
 * @return Entity object.
 */
public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
    Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
    return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
}
```

- We call `Objects.requireNonNull(position, …)` to match the use of `@NotNull` on the parameter.
- We look up `position` in the backing `map`.
- If no entity was ever put there, we return `new Empty()` so that queries outside of walls/boxes/players still behave as empty floor.

This fulfills the contract of `getEntity` and allows the rest of the game logic to run without throwing a `NotImplementedException`.

```java
	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();

			String row = lines[y];
			for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {

				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					map.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '.':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;

					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						if (players.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						players.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
						}
						boxes.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (players.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}

		for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
			char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
			if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
			}

		for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
			char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
			if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
	}
```

```java
	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
			String row = lines[y];
			for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
				char c = row.charAt(x);
				Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					map.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '.':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				case '@':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						if (players.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						players.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
						}
						boxes.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (players.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
					+ ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
			char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
			if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
			}
		}
		for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
			char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
			if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	 */
	public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
```

/**
```java
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.

public class GameMap {

	private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

	private final int maxWidth;

	private final int maxHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private final int undoLimit;

	/**
	 * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
	 *
	 * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
	 * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
	 * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
	 * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
	 *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
	 *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
	 *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
	 */
	public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
		this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.map = new HashMap<>();
	}

	private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
		this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
```
```java
	}

	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
			String row = lines[y];
			for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
				char c = row.charAt(x);
				Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					map.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '.':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				case '@':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						if (players.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						players.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
						}
						boxes.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (players.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
					+ ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
			char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
			if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
			}
		}
		for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
			char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
			if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity object at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
	 * @return  Entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
	 * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
	 * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
	 */
	public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		Objects.requireNonNull(entity, "entity must not be null");
		if (position.x() < 0 || position.x() >= maxWidth || position.y() < 0 || position.y() >= maxHeight) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(
					"Position " + position + " is out of bounds [0," + maxWidth + ")×[0," + maxHeight + ")");
		}
		map.put(position, entity);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all box destination positions as a set in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions.
	 */
	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return destinations;
	}
}
```

I didn’t find any existing references or tests for `getPlayerIds`, so we just need to follow its Javadoc:

> Get all players' id as a set.

Internally, a `GameMap` keeps a `Map<Position, Entity> map;`, and all player entities there are instances of `Player` (whose constructor takes an `int` id). So we should scan through `map.values()`, filter for `Player`, call `Player::getId()`, and collect into a `Set<Integer>`.

Here is a straightforward implementation of the `getPlayerIds` method:

```java
/**
 * Get all players' id as a set.
 *
 * @return a set of player id.
 */
public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
    return map.values().stream()
              .filter(e -> e instanceof Player)
              .map(e -> ((Player) e).getId())
              .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
}
```

3. **Extract IDs**: cast each to `Player` and call `getId()`
4. **Collect to set**: `Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet()`

```java
		Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
			String row = lines[y];
			for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
				char c = row.charAt(x);
				Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					map.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '.':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				case '@':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						if (players.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						players.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
						}
						boxes.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (players.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
					+ ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
			char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
			if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
			}
		}
		for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
			char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
			if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity object at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
	 * @return  Entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
	 * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
	 * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
	 */
	public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		Objects.requireNonNull(entity, "entity must not be null");
		if (position.x() < 0 || position.x() >= maxWidth || position.y() < 0 || position.y() >= maxHeight) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(
					"Position " + position + " is out of bounds [0," + maxWidth + ")×[0," + maxHeight + ")");
		}
		map.put(position, entity);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all box destination positions as a set in the game map.
	 * @return  a set of positions.
	 */
	@NotNull
	@Unmodifiable
	public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
		return destinations;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the undo limit of the game map.
	 * @return  undo limit.
	 */
	public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
		return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
	}
```

	/**
	 * Get all players' id as a set.
```java
	 * @return  a set of player id.
	 */
	public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
		return map.values().stream().filter(e -> e instanceof Player).map(e -> ((Player) e).getId())
				.collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
	}
}
```

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

	private final Map<Position, Entity> map;

	private final int maxWidth;

	private final int maxHeight;

	private final Set<Position> destinations;

	private final int undoLimit;

	/**
	 * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
	 *
	 * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
	 * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
	 * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
	 * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
	 *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
	 *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
	 *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
	 */
	public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
		this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.map = new HashMap<>();
	}

	private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
		this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
		this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
		this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
		this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
		this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
	}

	/**
	 * Get the maximum height of the game map.
	 *
	 * @return maximum height.
	 */
	public int getMaxHeight() {
		// TODO
		throw new NotImplementedException();
	}

	public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
		String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
		if (lines.length < 2) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
		}
		int undoLimit;
		try {
			undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
		}
		if (undoLimit < -1) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
		}
		Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
		Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
		Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
		Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();
		for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
			String row = lines[y];
			for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
				char c = row.charAt(x);
				Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
				switch (c) {
				case '#':
					map.put(pos, new Wall());
					break;
				case '.':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					break;
				case '@':
					map.put(pos, new Empty());
					destinations.add(pos);
					break;
				default:
					if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
						if (players.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
						}
						players.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
					} else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
						if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
						}
						boxes.put(c, pos);
						map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
					} else {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (players.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
		}
		if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
					+ ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
		}
		for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
			char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
			if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
			}
		}
		for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
			char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
			if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
			}
		}
		return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
	}

	/**
	 * Get the entity object at the given position.
	 * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
	 * @return  Entity object.
	 */
	public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
	}

	/**
	 * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
	 * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
	 * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
	 */
	public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		Objects.requireNonNull(entity, "entity must not be null");
		if (position.x() < 0 || position.x() >= maxWidth || position.y() < 0 || position.y() >= maxHeight) {
```

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.actions.Move;
import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import assignment.entities.Wall;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Unmodifiable;

import java.util.*;
import java.util.stream.Collectors;

/**
 * A Sokoban game board.
 * GameBoard consists of information loaded from map data, such as
 * <li>Width and height of the game map</li>
 * <li>Walls in the map</li>
 * <li>Box destinations</li>
 * <li>Initial locations of boxes and player</li>
 * <p/>
 * GameBoard is capable to create many GameState instances, each representing an ongoing game.
 */
public class GameMap {

    private final Map<Position, Entity> map;
    private final int maxWidth;
    private final int maxHeight;
    private final Set<Position> destinations;
    private final int undoLimit;

    /**
     * Create a new GameMap with width, height, set of box destinations and undo limit.
     *
     * @param maxWidth     Width of the game map.
     * @param maxHeight    Height of the game map.
     * @param destinations Set of box destination positions.
     * @param undoLimit    Undo limit.
     *                     Positive numbers specify the maximum number of undo actions.
     *                     0 means undo is not allowed.
     *                     -1 means unlimited. Other negative numbers are not allowed.
     */
    public GameMap(int maxWidth, int maxHeight, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.maxWidth = maxWidth;
        this.maxHeight = maxHeight;
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.map = new HashMap<>();
    }

    private GameMap(Map<Position, Entity> map, Set<Position> destinations, int undoLimit) {
        this.map = Collections.unmodifiableMap(map);
        this.destinations = Collections.unmodifiableSet(destinations);
        this.undoLimit = undoLimit;
        this.maxWidth = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::x).max().orElse(0) + 1;
        this.maxHeight = map.keySet().stream().mapToInt(Position::y).max().orElse(0) + 1;
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum height of the game map.
     *
     * @return maximum height.
     */
    public int getMaxHeight() {
```
        return maxHeight;
    }

```java
    public static GameMap parse(String mapText) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(mapText, "mapText must not be null");
        String[] lines = mapText.split("\\R", -1);
        if (lines.length < 2) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must have at least an undo limit and one map line");
        }
        int undoLimit;
        try {
            undoLimit = Integer.parseInt(lines[0].trim());
        } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("First line must be an integer undo limit", e);
        }
        if (undoLimit < -1) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Undo limit must be -1 (unlimited) or non-negative");
        }
        Map<Position, Entity> map = new HashMap<>();
        Set<Position> destinations = new HashSet<>();
        Map<Character, Position> players = new HashMap<>();
        Map<Character, Position> boxes = new HashMap<>();
        for (int y = 1; y < lines.length; y++) {
            String row = lines[y];
            for (int x = 0; x < row.length(); x++) {
                char c = row.charAt(x);
                Position pos = new Position(x, y - 1);
                switch (c) {
                    case '#':
                        map.put(pos, new Wall());
                        break;
                    case '.':
                        map.put(pos, new Empty());
                        break;
                    case '@':
                        map.put(pos, new Empty());
                        destinations.add(pos);
                        break;
                    default:
                        if (Character.isUpperCase(c)) {
                            if (players.containsKey(c)) {
                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate player '" + c + "'");
                            }
                            players.put(c, pos);
                            map.put(pos, new Player(c - 'A'));
                        } else if (Character.isLowerCase(c)) {
                            if (boxes.containsKey(c)) {
                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Duplicate box '" + c + "'");
                            }
                            boxes.put(c, pos);
                            map.put(pos, new Box(c - 'a'));
                        } else {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid character '" + c + "' in map");
                        }
                }
            }
        }
        if (players.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must contain at least one player");
        }
        if (boxes.size() != destinations.size()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Number of boxes (" + boxes.size()
                    + ") does not match number of destinations (" + destinations.size() + ")");
        }
        for (char bc : boxes.keySet()) {
            char pc = Character.toUpperCase(bc);
            if (!players.containsKey(pc)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Box '" + bc + "' has no matching player '" + pc + "'");
            }
        }
        for (char pc : players.keySet()) {
            char bc = Character.toLowerCase(pc);
            if (!boxes.containsKey(bc)) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Player '" + pc + "' has no matching box '" + bc + "'");
            }
        }
        return new GameMap(map, destinations, undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get the entity object at the given position.
     * @param position  the position of the entity in the game map.
     * @return  Entity object.
     */
    public Entity getEntity(@NotNull Position position) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        return map.getOrDefault(position, new Empty());
    }

    /**
     * Put one entity at the given position in the game map.
     * @param position  the position in the game map to put the entity.
     * @param entity    the entity to put into game map.
     */
    public void putEntity(Position position, Entity entity) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
        Objects.requireNonNull(entity, "entity must not be null");
        if (position.x() < 0 || position.x() >= maxWidth || position.y() < 0 || position.y() >= maxHeight) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Position " + position + " is out of bounds [0," + maxWidth + ")×[0," + maxHeight + ")");
        }
        map.put(position, entity);
    }

    /**
     * Get all box destination positions as a set in the game map.
     * @return  a set of positions.
     */
    @NotNull
    @Unmodifiable
    public Set<Position> getDestinations() {
        return destinations;
    }

    /**
     * Get the undo limit of the game map.
     * @return  undo limit.
     */
    public Optional<Integer> getUndoLimit() {
        return undoLimit < 0 ? Optional.empty() : Optional.of(undoLimit);
    }

    /**
     * Get all players' id as a set.
     * @return  a set of player id.
     */
    public Set<Integer> getPlayerIds() {
        return map.values().stream().filter(e -> e instanceof Player)
```
```java
                  .map(e -> ((Player) e).getId())
                  .collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableSet());
    }

    /**
     * Get the maximum width of the game map.
     * @return  maximum width.
     */
    public int getMaxWidth() {
        return maxWidth;
    }
}
```

```java
package assignment.game;

import assignment.entities.Box;
import assignment.entities.Empty;
import assignment.entities.Entity;
import assignment.entities.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Optional;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * The state of the Sokoban Game.
 * Each game state represents an ongoing game.
 * As the game goes, the game state changes while players are moving
 * while the original game map stays unmodified.
 */
public class GameState {

    private final Stack<Transition> history = new Stack<>();
    private final Map<Position, Entity> entities;
    private final int boardWidth;
    private final int boardHeight;
    private final Set<Position> destinations;
    private int undoQuota;
    private Transition currentTransition = new Transition();

    /**
     * Create a running game state from a game map.
     *
     * @param map the game map from which to create this game state.
     */
    public GameState(@NotNull GameMap map) {
        // board dimensions
        this.boardWidth  = map.getWidth();
        this.boardHeight = map.getHeight();

        // copy destinations
        this.destinations = Set.copyOf(map.getDestinations());

        // initialize mutable entities map
        this.entities = new HashMap<>();

        // populate entities from map, but never modify the original GameMap
        for (int y = 0; y < boardHeight; y++) {
            for (int x = 0; x < boardWidth; x++) {
                Position pos = new Position(x, y);
                Entity e = map.getEntity(pos);
                // walls never move, so omit them
                switch (e.getType()) {
                    case BOX:
                        entities.put(pos, new Box());
                        break;
                    case PLAYER:
                        Player p = (Player) e;
                        entities.put(pos, new Player(p.getId()));
                        break;
                    case EMPTY:
                        entities.put(pos, new Empty());
                        break;
                    default:
                        // skip walls or unsupported types
                }
            }
        }

        // set undo quota (empty = unlimited)
        this.undoQuota = map.getUndoLimit().orElse(Integer.MAX_VALUE);
    }
    // … other methods …
}
```
【F:assignment/game/GameState.java†L35-L76】

**Explanation of the key steps:**

1. **Dimensions and Destinations**  
   We read `map.getWidth()/getHeight()` to record the board size and copy `map.getDestinations()` into an unmodifiable `Set`.

2. **Entity Initialization**  
   We iterate every `(x,y)` on the board, call `map.getEntity(pos)`, and recreate a fresh `Box`, `Player`, or `Empty` in our local `entities` map (omitting walls entirely, since walls never move).  This ensures we never modify the original `GameMap`’s internal state.

3. **Undo Quota**  
   If the map’s undo limit is `Optional.empty()`, we treat it as “unlimited” by using `Integer.MAX_VALUE`; otherwise we use the provided limit.

This constructor gives you a clean, mutable game‐state backed by the original (immutable) `GameMap`.

## Proposed implementation

```java
/**
 * Get the current position of the player with the given id.
 *
 * @param id player id.
 * @return the current position of the player.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if no player with the given id is present.
 */
public Position getPlayerPositionById(int id) {
    return entities.entrySet().stream()
        .filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player p && p.id() == id)
        .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
        .findAny()
        .orElseThrow(() -> new IllegalArgumentException(
            "No player found with id " + id));
}
```

4. Return any matching position or throw if none found.

Response Text:---
Below is a concise implementation of **`getAllPlayerPositions`** in **`GameState`**, together with a brief rationale.

---

### Brief explanation

The game‐state keeps a map from each occupied **`Position`** to its current **`Entity`** (boxes, players, empties, …). To collect all player positions, we simply scan through the **`entities`** map, filter for those entries whose value is an instance of **`Player`**, and collect their keys (the positions) into an unmodifiable **`Set<Position>`**.

---

### Method implementation

```java
/**
 * Get current positions of all players in the game map.
 *
 * @return a set of positions of all players.
 */
@Unmodifiable
public Set<Position> getAllPlayerPositions() {
    return Collections.unmodifiableSet(
        entities.entrySet().stream()
                .filter(e -> e.getValue() instanceof Player)
                .map(Map.Entry::getKey)
                .collect(Collectors.toSet())
    );
}
```
【F:src/assignment/game/GameState.java†L49-L57】

---

#### Notes

1. We return an **unmodifiable** set to prevent callers from mutating the game state.
2. We rely on the fact that **`entities`** is a **`Map<Position,Entity>`** holding the current occupants of every square on the board.
3. We use Java 19 features (stream API) consistently with the rest of the class.

This completes the `getAllPlayerPositions` method so that your Sokoban game will correctly report where all players currently stand.

Response Text:---
Below is a simple implementation of `isWin()` that returns `true` exactly when every destination square is currently occupied by a box (i.e. the `Entity` at each destination is an instance of `Box`).

```java
/**
 * Check whether the game wins or not.
 * The game wins only when all box destinations have been occupied by boxes.
 *
 * @return true iff the game is won.
 */
public boolean isWin() {
    // every destination must hold a Box
    return destinations.stream()
                       .allMatch(pos -> entities.get(pos) instanceof Box);
}
```
【F:src/main/java/assignment/game/GameState.java†L48-L56】

**Explanation:**  
We keep track of all “box destination” positions in the `destinations` set.  In the current game state we store which `Entity` (like a `Box`, `Empty`, etc.) sits on each `Position` in the `entities` map.  We simply check that for every position in `destinations`, the corresponding `Entity` is a `Box`.

It looks like your project already defines how moves are recorded and applied via the internal `Transition` and undo machinery. In your `GameState` class you only need to:

1.  Record the “from→to” positions into the current (in‑flight) `Transition`.
2.  Update the `entities` map so that whatever was at `from` moves to `to`, and the old `from` slot becomes an `Empty`.
3.  Push a `Move` action onto the current transition so that your external API (e.g. your move history) sees the same logical move.

Putting that together, here is a self‑contained implementation of `move(...)`.  (You don’t need to touch the rest of the class.)

```java
/**
 * Move the entity from one position to another.
 * This method assumes the validity of this move is ensured.
 * <b>The validity of the move of the entity in one position to another need not to check.</b>
 *
 * @param from The current position of the entity to move.
 * @param to   The position to move the entity to.
 */
public void move(Position from, Position to) {
    // 1. Record in the current Transition (so undo can reverse it)
    currentTransition.add(from, to);

    // 2. Perform the move in the entities map
    Entity e = entities.remove(from);
    entities.put(from, new Empty());
    entities.put(to, e);

    // 3. Record the high‑level Move action for history/logging
    history.push(new Transition());           // start a fresh transition for the next move
    history.peek().add(from, to);             // store the same from→to into the pushed transition
    currentTransition = new Transition();     // reset currentTransition for subsequent moves
}
```

**Explanation**

- We call `currentTransition.add(from,to)` so that when you do an undo, your code will know how to reverse this single step.
- We then remove the entity at `from`, replace it with an `Empty`, and put the entity back at `to`.
- Finally, we push a new `Transition` onto your `history` stack (wrapping the same `from→to`), and reset `currentTransition` so you can record the next discrete step correctly.

This satisfies your requirement without touching any other parts of the `GameState` class.

Response Text:---
I’m going to implement `GameState.checkpoint()`, which must snapshot (push) the current board‐entity positions and the undo quota onto the history stack so that a subsequent `undo()` can restore them.

---

### How `checkpoint()` should work

- Record both  
  1. the current mapping of `Position→Entity` (so we know where every box/player was), and  
  2. the current `undoQuota`  
- Push that snapshot onto the `history` stack as a new `Transition`‑like object (we’ll piggy‑back on `Transition` for storing positions).
- Reset any in‑flight moves in `currentTransition`.

Internally we’ll package positions into a fresh `Transition` instance, then push it together with the undo quota.

---

### Implementation of `checkpoint()`

```java
/**
 * Record a checkpoint of the game state, including:
 * <li>All current positions of entities in the game map.</li>
 * <li>Current undo quota</li>
 * <p>
 * Checkpoint is used in {@link GameState#undo()}.
 * Every undo actions reverts the game state to the last checkpoint.
 */
public void checkpoint() {
    // snapshot current undo quota first
    int quotaSnapshot = this.undoQuota;

    // snapshot all entities' positions as a Transition
    Transition snapshot = new Transition();
    for (var entry : this.entities.entrySet()) {
        Position pos = entry.getKey();
        // map each pos to itself to record its location
        snapshot.add(pos, pos);
    }

    // push a marker for undoQuota (we store quota in a negative (dummy) move to carry it)
    // we overload the Transition.moves to hold extra meta; here we stash the quota under null
    snapshot.moves.put(null, new Position(quotaSnapshot, 0));

    // push it onto history and reset currentTransition
    history.push(snapshot);
    currentTransition = new Transition();
}
```
